Resource.title: Resource
Resource.description: Represents a resource link in the directory, such as chants, songs, schedules, or announcements.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Resource entity.

description.description: A brief description of the resource.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category for grouping resources in the directory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: Name of the category (e.g., Chants, Songs, Schedules).

RosterEntry.title: RosterEntry
RosterEntry.description: Represents a single entry in the weekly volunteer/staff roster.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RosterEntry entity.

volunteerName.description: Name of the volunteer or staff member.

role.description: The role assigned to the volunteer/staff for the week.

date.description: The date for which the roster entry is valid.

Announcement.title: Announcement
Announcement.description: Represents an announcement to be displayed in the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Announcement entity.

content.description: The main text content of the announcement.

date.description: Date the announcement was created or is relevant to.

Video.title: Video
Video.description: Represents a video to be displayed in the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Video entity.

description.description: A brief description of the video.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the NDC Preschooler's Church application, focusing on resource directory, roster management, and content management features. To ensure security and scalability, we adhere to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and Rules-are-not-Filters (QAPs).  

**Authorization Independence:** Authorization is achieved by avoiding hierarchical `get()` calls. While the relationships exist in the application (e.g., a `Category` has many `Resources`), the security rules do not rely on fetching parent documents to authorize access to child documents.  

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):** Each collection is designed to have a clear and consistent security posture. For instance, all documents within the `categories` collection share the same access control requirements.

**Access Modeling:**
*   **RosterEntry and Announcement:** Data is considered globally accessible by authenticated users, as required by the use case.  Admin priviledges are handled by the `roles_admin` collection.
*   **Category and Resource:** Data is considered globally accessible by authenticated users, as required by the use case. Admin priviledges are handled by the `roles_admin` collection.
*   **Video:** Data is considered globally accessible by authenticated users, as required by the use case. Admin priviledges are handled by the `roles_admin` collection.

**QAPs Support (Rules are not Filters):** The structure enables secure `list` operations. Since all documents in a collection share the same security posture, listing documents does not require filtering based on authorization logic within the rules themselves, promoting efficient and secure data retrieval.

**Global Roles (DBAC):** Administrative privileges are managed using the `roles_admin` collection. The existence of a document with a user's UID in this collection grants admin access, adhering to the principle of "Existence over Content."
